title: Bipartite edge frustration of nut graphs: proofs and constructions
summary: The bipartite edge frustration of a graph $G$, $\varphi(G)$, is the minimum number of edges that must be removed from $G$ to obtain a graph that is bipartite. Core graphs are singular graphs on $2$ or more vertices, for which the kernel of the adjacency matrix contains a full eigenvector. A nut graph is a core graph of nullity one. Nut graphs $G$ are non-bipartite. It is proved here that $\varphi(G) \geq 2$ if $G$ is a nut graph, i.e. every nut graph requires deletion of at least two edges to produce a bipartite graph.
